title: Exact sheet-return equivalence with the specified Weil structure
statement: Fix a finite-field datum D [def-weil-finite-field-fiber], an integer m≥1, a separated finite-type k₀-scheme X₀, a prime ℓ≠p and an algebraic closure Ω of Q_ℓ with the common-stage coefficients of [def-weil-algebraically-closed-coefficients]. In the actual common-stage constructible Weil hearts [def-weil-constructible-heart], [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], there exists a functor R from Weil sheaves on X₀×k₀ k_m regarded over k₀ to Weil sheaves on the same scheme over k_m, which is an equivalence and satisfies ConstantExtensionSheetSpec [def-zl-constant-extension-sheet-pullback-data]: its carrier is distinguished-sheet pullback and its Weil structure is exactly the ordered m-fold iterate with the specified compositors. No weight or local-operator assertion is part of this lemma.

source.place: (1.1.7)--(1.1.10), pp. 150--152, and (1.2.6), p. 154; ordered block and finite-filtration consequences.

proof.text: The constructible-heart statement identifies the underlying category as abelian. Use the sheet-coordinate equivalence on constructible hearts, with $A_i=(H^ij_0)^*N$ and arrows $a_i$ as in the cited coordinate statement. Apply the cited cyclic-return equivalence with $\mathcal C=\operatorname{Sh}_c(X,\Qlb)$ and the exact autoequivalence $P=Lg_X^*$. Its return is $(A_0,a_0\cdots a_{m-1})$, precisely $(j_0^*N,\phi)$ with the specified pullback compositors. On morphisms it is $u_0=j_0^*u$. Thus $R$ is a functor and an exact equivalence; in particular it identifies subobjects, quotients and finite filtrations in both directions. This uses the two cited statements, not the parent constant-extension equivalence (which depends on the present item).
